# plugin-hostd / fuzz_command

plugin-hostd's own fuzz target `fuzz_command` ([source](source/fuzz_command.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over plugin-hostd 0.10.0 (FreeMixer/plugin-hostd at 65cd2b02).

Reads the input as up to 32 messages, each a flags byte, a two-byte length and up to 8192 bytes, copies each into an allocation of exactly its length and hands it to verbs_receive, plugin-hostd's command parser and dispatcher. A recorder stands in for the supervisor, the pins, the descriptor scans and the socket: it records every call and, as the flags byte chooses, accepts it with the verb's declared reply or refuses it with a declared error code. After each message the harness checks the reply and the calls, then sends the message again as its words joined by one space.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libplugin-hostd.a of src/verbs.c of plugin-hostd 0.10.0 at commit 65cd2b02 and the harness's recorder, fuzz/recorder.c, compiled with mod-host's protocol headers as FreeMixer ships them, as plugin-hostd's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Every message gets exactly one reply, a NUL-terminated string with no earlier NUL. When a recorded call answered, the reply is that answer unchanged; otherwise it is a refusal or the "resp 0" of quit. A refusal is "resp <code>" of a declared error code, and any other reply has the shape its verb declares or mod-host's "resp 0" ([lines 199-259](source/fuzz_command.c#L199-L259)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A verb the daemon parses itself (its own verbs, and mod-host's remove, connect, disconnect and quit) is acted on only with an argument count its declared syntax allows, counting at most 64 words; a line passed on to every worker for the workers to refuse is exempt ([lines 271-297](source/fuzz_command.c#L271-L297)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each recorded call gets the message's words where the verb's declaration puts them (as written, as atoi reads them, or the whole line with single spaces), and add's placement and client, chain's members and their count, and pin_set's verdict are the ones the harness works out from the words. Other arguments are not checked ([lines 299-444](source/fuzz_command.c#L299-L444)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A refused command (a reply with a negative code) leaves the recorded state as it was: no accepted call, no descriptor scan or other follow-up, and no quit ([lines 446-456](source/fuzz_command.c#L446-L456)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A command the daemon acted on, sent again from the same state as its words joined by one space, makes the same calls with the same arguments, the same reply, the same state and host settings, and quits the same ([lines 458-503](source/fuzz_command.c#L458-L503)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The reply shape each verb declares, filled in, fits one line of the protocol (4096 bytes) ([lines 263-267](source/recorder.c#L263-L267)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch plugin-hostd` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
